Description: Define layout and visuals in XAML not code-behind
Do: XAML for structure and styling
Don't: Build UI trees in C# code-behind

Description: Connects XAML to its code-behind partial class
Do: x:Class on Window UserControl and Page

Description: Only name elements accessed from code-behind
Do: x:Name when code-behind reference is needed

Description: Grid.Row Grid.Column DockPanel.Dock etc
Do: Attached properties for panel positioning

Description: Enable UI updates when properties change
Do: INotifyPropertyChanged on ViewModels
Code Good: public string Name { get => _name; set { _name = value; OnPropertyChanged(); } }
Code Bad: public string Name { get; set; } without notification

Description: Notifies UI of add remove and reset
Do: ObservableCollection<T> for bound collections
Don't: List<T> or Array for bound ItemsSources

Guideline: Set DataContext at the right level
Description: Enables binding for the visual subtree
Do: DataContext on Window or root container
Code Bad: Setting DataContext on each TextBlock individually

Description: Declarative binding keeps UI and logic separate
Do: {Binding Path=Name} in XAML
Code Bad: Loaded event handler that sets every property

Description: Controls when source updates
Do: PropertyChanged for real-time validation
Don't: Default LostFocus when instant feedback needed

Description: Convert data for presentation without changing the model
Do: IValueConverter for bool-to-visibility etc
Code Bad: public Visibility IsActiveVisibility => IsActive ? Visibility.Visible : Visibility.Collapsed;

Description: Avoid converters for basic string formatting
Do: StringFormat in Binding for dates currency etc
Code Bad: Custom converter just to add a dollar sign

Description: Handle null or missing binding gracefully
Do: FallbackValue for design-time and missing paths
Code Bad: No fallback leading to blank fields

Description: Rows and columns with proportional or fixed sizing
Do: Grid with RowDefinitions and ColumnDefinitions
Don't: Canvas with absolute positions for forms

Description: Simple vertical or horizontal stacking
Do: StackPanel for toolbars and simple lists
Don't: Grid with single column for linear content

Description: Dock children to edges with last child filling
Do: DockPanel for shell layouts (menu top sidebar left)
Code Bad: Nested StackPanels with fixed widths for shell

Description: All cells share the same size
Do: UniformGrid for icon grids and dashboards

Description: Use Auto Star and MinWidth/MaxWidth
Do: Proportional sizing with * and Auto
Don't: Fixed pixel widths on resizable content

Description: Wrap content that may exceed available space
Do: ScrollViewer around long forms or lists

Description: Centralize colors brushes and styles
Do: ResourceDictionary in App.xaml for theme values
Don't: Inline colors and font sizes on every element

Description: Apply a Style to all instances of a TargetType
Do: Style with TargetType and no x:Key for defaults

Description: Named styles for specific variants
Do: x:Key styles for variant controls
Don't: Implicit style overrides for special cases
Code Bad: Duplicating full implicit style for one override

Description: Extend styles without duplication
Do: BasedOn to inherit from implicit or named styles
Code Bad: Copy-pasting 10 Setters into a second Style

Description: StaticResource is resolved once and faster
Do: StaticResource for values that do not change at runtime
Code Bad: Background="{DynamicResource PrimaryBrush}" when theme never changes

Description: Override default rendering of a control
Do: ControlTemplate when built-in styles are insufficient
Don't: Nesting extra panels to hide the default template
Code Bad: Wrapping Button in Border to fake a custom look

Description: Define how data objects render in ItemsControls
Do: DataTemplate for ListBox ComboBox and ItemsControl items

Description: Decouple UI actions from logic
Do: ICommand implementations (RelayCommand DelegateCommand)

Description: Automatically disable controls when action unavailable
Do: CanExecute returning false to disable buttons
Don't: IsEnabled binding to a separate bool

Description: Avoid implementing ICommand from scratch every time
Do: RelayCommand from CommunityToolkit.Mvvm or Prism
Code Bad: class SaveCommand : ICommand { ... } for each action

Description: Pass data from the UI element to the command handler
Do: CommandParameter for item-specific actions
Don't: Relying on SelectedItem in every command

Description: ApplicationCommands for Cut Copy Paste Save etc
Do: RoutedCommands with InputBindings for keyboard shortcuts

Description: Only creates UI elements for visible items
Do: VirtualizingStackPanel.IsVirtualizing=True (default in ListBox)

Description: Frozen brushes and geometries skip change tracking
Do: Freeze brushes and pens that do not change
Don't: Mutable brushes used as static resources
Code Bad: new SolidColorBrush() without Freeze in resources

Description: Binding to CLR properties uses reflection
Do: Bind to DependencyProperties when possible
Don't: Binding to plain CLR properties in custom controls
Code Bad: public string Name { get; set; } as binding target on custom control

Description: Keep UI thread responsive
Do: async/await with Task.Run for CPU work
Don't: Synchronous operations that freeze the UI

Description: Defer content scroll for heavy items
Do: ScrollViewer.IsDeferredScrollingEnabled for complex items
Don't: Immediate scroll with heavy item templates

Guideline: Profile with PerfView and Visual Studio
Description: Measure before optimizing
Do: Visual Studio diagnostic tools and PerfView

Description: UI elements can only be accessed from the UI thread
Do: Dispatcher.Invoke or BeginInvoke from background threads
Don't: Accessing UI elements from background threads

Description: Modern async code returns to UI context automatically
Do: async/await which resumes on captured SynchronizationContext
Code Good: var data = await LoadDataAsync(); Items = data;

Guideline: Use BackgroundWorker or Task.Run for CPU work
Description: Offload intensive work from UI thread
Do: Task.Run for compute-bound work
Code Bad: var result = Compute(); on UI thread

Description: Update UI with progress during long operations
Do: IProgress<T> with Task.Run
Don't: Polling a shared variable for progress
Code Good: var progress = new Progress<int>(p => ProgressBar.Value = p); await Task.Run(() => Work(progress));

Description: Enable screen reader support
Do: AutomationProperties.Name on interactive controls

Description: All functionality reachable via keyboard
Do: Tab order and KeyboardNavigation properties
Code Bad: Click handlers with no keyboard equivalent

Description: Respect Windows high contrast settings
Do: SystemColors and SystemFonts resources
Don't: Hardcoded colors that disappear in high contrast

Description: Semantic controls convey role to assistive tech
Do: Button for actions CheckBox for toggles
Don't: Styled TextBlock with click handler as fake button

Description: Ensure UI is crisp at all display scale factors
Do: Device-independent units and vector graphics
Don't: Pixel-based bitmaps that blur at high DPI

Description: Separate View ViewModel and Model concerns
Do: MVVM with data binding and commands

Description: Register and resolve services via DI container
Do: IServiceProvider with Microsoft.Extensions.DI

Description: Source generators reduce MVVM boilerplate
Do: [ObservableProperty] and [RelayCommand] attributes
Code Bad: private string _name; public string Name { get ... set ... OnPropertyChanged ... }

Description: Code-behind should only contain view-specific logic
Do: View logic like focus management and animations in code-behind
Don't: Business logic and data access in code-behind
Code Good: Loaded handler that sets initial focus
Code Bad: Loaded handler that calls database and populates grid

Description: Communicate between ViewModels without references
Do: WeakReferenceMessenger from CommunityToolkit.Mvvm

Description: Test business logic independent of UI
Do: xUnit or NUnit tests on ViewModel methods and properties
Don't: Manual testing through the UI only
Code Bad: Clicking buttons in the running app to verify

Description: Isolate ViewModel from external dependencies
Do: Moq or NSubstitute for service interfaces
Don't: Real database calls in unit tests
Code Good: var mock = new Mock<IDataService>(); var vm = new MainViewModel(mock.Object);

Guideline: Use UI Automation for integration tests
Description: Automated UI testing with Microsoft UI Automation
Do: Coded UI or Appium for end-to-end tests

Description: Converters have logic that can break
Do: Unit tests calling Convert and ConvertBack directly
